fields.description:
## Context
Cut the next fix release, 0.13.1, from reviewed main using docs/releasing.md. Prior
package/tag: 0.13.0/v0.13.0 (currently live on PyPI and the latest GitHub Release). Only
6 commits landed on main since v0.13.0, all internal/non-user-facing (config/plan_review
split, SSM secret handling, MCP registry description-length fix, LLM cache/enrichment
tweaks) -- CHANGELOG.md's [Unreleased] section on origin/main is empty, so step 1a is a
no-op retitle/placeholder rather than a curated entry. PyPI is immutable; publication uses
the dispatch-from-main workflow and its pypi environment approval.

Known risk: ticket hyperbolic-pernicious-drongo (0.13.0) closed FAILED because, after PyPI
publish succeeded in one release.yml run, the mcp_registry job failed (server.json
description length); by the time the fix landed, PyPI 0.13.0 was immutable so the workflow
could not be re-dispatched (400 File already exists), and the documented manual
mcp-publisher fallback was blocked by a navapbc org OAuth-App access restriction needing
org-admin action. The registry still reports 0.12.0 as isLatest. Mitigation: before
dispatch, confirm that OAuth-App restriction is resolved so the manual fallback is usable if
mcp_registry fails again post-publish. If it still cannot be made to report 0.13.1 after
exhausting both paths, close with that one AC marked [non-codebase, known-blocked] plus a
linked follow-up ticket, rather than yanking the already-live PyPI/GitHub Release for a
registry-only gap.

## Plan
- Fresh worktree from origin/main; confirm prerequisites, identity, Gerrit rights, channel
  state, and the navapbc OAuth-App access posture (mitigation above).
- Bump pyproject.toml + every server.json version to 0.13.1; regenerate uv.lock; add a
  0.13.1 CHANGELOG section (today's date) via the changelog generator as a starting point,
  hand-curated, with a fresh empty Unreleased section and updated compare links.
- Regenerate tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json (__version__ bump), the step the 0.13.0
  release ticket documented as newly required.
- Preflight: version-lockstep guard, release-specific tests, lint, typecheck, full test
  suite, build, and twine check of the artifacts.
- Commit with DCO + Change-Id + rebar-ticket trailer; push to Gerrit; earn LLM-Review +1 and
  Verified +1 with no unresolved comments; Submit.
- Dispatch release.yml from main with version=0.13.1; approve the pypi environment
  deployment; monitor to completion, watching mcp_registry given the prior failure there.
- Verify PyPI + PEP 740 provenance, GitHub tag/release + artifacts, MCP Registry (confirm
  0.13.1 isLatest), and the Homebrew tap bump.
- Channel-install nava-rebar[mcp]==0.13.1 and run the packaged post-publication probe.
- Record receipts; close only once all acceptance criteria are met (or the one documented
  registry exception above applies).

## File impact
- pyproject.toml -- package version bump
- server.json -- MCP manifest/package version bump
- uv.lock -- root package version lockstep with pyproject.toml
- CHANGELOG.md -- new 0.13.1 release section and compare links
- tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json -- __version__ bump

## Rollback / failure policy
Before publish: stop on any failed guard/review/CI vote; remediate via a new Gerrit
patchset. After publish, PyPI cannot be replaced: yank 0.13.1, de-list its GitHub Release,
and cut a fixed next patch version; never overwrite artifacts or retag published content.
If PyPI/GitHub Release publish succeeds but mcp_registry fails and the manual fallback is
also blocked (the exact 0.13.0 failure mode): do not yank the already-live PyPI/GitHub
Release artifacts for this reason alone; record the gap as a documented, linked follow-up
and mark the corresponding acceptance criterion [non-codebase, known-blocked] rather than
leaving the ticket in limbo.

## Testing
- Run the version-lockstep release guard script against pyproject.toml and server.json with
  version 0.13.1 and confirm it exits 0.
- Run "make lint", "make typecheck", and "make test" under the worktree virtualenv and
  confirm each exits 0.
- Run "python -m build" to produce the 0.13.1 wheel and sdist, then "python -m twine check"
  against the built artifacts and confirm it exits 0.
- Run the pypi-attestations verifier against the published 0.13.1 wheel, scoped to the
  navapbc/rebar repository, and confirm it exits 0.
- Install the channel-published nava-rebar[mcp]==0.13.1 build and run the packaged
  scripts/probe_rebar.py probe against it, confirming zero failures.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] pyproject.toml declares version 0.13.1.
- [x] server.json top-level version is 0.13.1.
- [x] Every server.json packages[].version is 0.13.1.
- [x] uv.lock records the root nava-rebar package at version 0.13.1.
- [x] Running "uv lock --check" exits 0.
- [x] CHANGELOG.md contains a 0.13.1 section dated with today's release date.
- [x] CHANGELOG.md has a fresh Unreleased section and correct 0.13.1 compare links.
- [x] tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json reflects __version__ 0.13.1.
- [x] The release_guards.py version-lockstep check exits 0 for version 0.13.1 against
      pyproject.toml and server.json.
- [x] The release-specific guard and workflow pin unit tests
      (tests/unit/test_release_guards.py and tests/unit/test_release_workflow_pins.py) all pass.
- [x] "make lint" exits 0 under the worktree virtualenv.
- [x] "make typecheck" exits 0 under the worktree virtualenv.
- [x] "make test" exits 0 under the worktree virtualenv.
- [x] "python -m build" produces the 0.13.1 wheel and sdist.
- [x] "python -m twine check" exits 0 for the built artifacts.
- [x] The release commit contains DCO sign-off, a Gerrit Change-Id, and this rebar-ticket
      trailer.
- [x] Gerrit records LLM-Review +1 on the release change.
- [x] Gerrit records Verified +1 on the release change.
- [x] Gerrit has no unresolved comments on the release change.
- [x] Gerrit submits the release change and the resulting commit is on main.
- [x] release.yml is dispatched from main with version input 0.13.1.
- [x] The required pypi environment deployment is approved.
- [x] Every required release.yml job completes successfully (build, wheel_test, sdist_test,
      publish, mcp_verify, mcp_registry, github_release).
- [x] PyPI serves nava-rebar 0.13.1.
- [x] [non-codebase] The pypi-attestations verifier passes against the published 0.13.1
      wheel scoped to the navapbc/rebar repository.
      provenance: environment=local-macos-shell; principal=joeoakhart@navapbc.com; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — downloaded the published wheel from files.pythonhosted.org and ran `pypi-attestations verify pypi nava_rebar-0.13.1-py3-none-any.whl --repository https://github.com/navapbc/rebar`, which printed "OK: nava_rebar-0.13.1-py3-none-any.whl".
- [x] [non-codebase] GitHub tag v0.13.1 resolves to the released main commit.
      provenance: environment=local-macos-shell; principal=joeoakhart@navapbc.com; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — `gh release view v0.13.1 --repo navapbc/rebar` returned tagName=v0.13.1, publishedAt=2026-08-30T03:33:58Z, targeting the commit created by the release.yml github_release job off main.
- [x] [non-codebase] GitHub Release v0.13.1 is marked Latest and attaches the 0.13.1 wheel
      and sdist.
      provenance: environment=local-macos-shell; principal=joeoakhart@navapbc.com; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — `gh release list --repo navapbc/rebar` shows v0.13.1 flagged "Latest"; release.yml's github_release job (which attaches the build-once wheel/sdist) completed successfully in run 33290369748.
- [x] [non-codebase, known-blocked-risk] MCP Registry reports io.github.navapbc/rebar
      version 0.13.1 as isLatest, or (if blocked by the known OAuth-App restriction even
      after the mitigation above) a linked follow-up ticket documents the gap and this item
      is explicitly marked as the accepted exception.
      provenance: environment=local-macos-shell; principal=joeoakhart@navapbc.com; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — GET https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers?search=rebar shows the io.github.navapbc/rebar entry at version=0.13.1 with isLatest=true, status=active (no exception needed; the mcp_registry job in release.yml run 33290369748 succeeded, unlike the 0.13.0 release).
- [x] [non-codebase] Homebrew tap Formula/rebar.rb points to the 0.13.1 PyPI sdist URL with
      matching SHA-256 (or the scheduled autobump run is confirmed to have picked it up).
      provenance: environment=local-macos-shell; principal=joeoakhart@navapbc.com; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — manually dispatched navapbc/homebrew-rebar's "Autobump formula from PyPI" workflow (run 33290636554, success) since the scheduled poll predated the publish; confirmed via `gh api repos/navapbc/homebrew-rebar/contents/Formula/rebar.rb` that the formula's url/sha256 now reference nava_rebar-0.13.1.tar.gz and its matching PyPI-reported sha256.
- [x] A fresh channel install of nava-rebar[mcp]==0.13.1 passes scripts/probe_rebar.py with
      zero failures.
- [x] Release receipts, any exceptions, and the rollback disposition are recorded on this
      ticket.
